note: Draft vectors for LIP-0026. No vector holds a grant, a transaction or an entry of a journal: rows, limits, coins, inputs and requests are stated facts. Identifiers of grants and of requests, public keys, transaction ids and scripts are placeholders. A vector of the groups parents, fit and coins whose outcome is not the passing one holds one defect and names a neighbour with the passing outcome that differs from it in that defect; a vector marked compound holds two defects and names none. A trace of the group ledgers states the outcome of each request and the accounts at its end, and names no neighbour. The refusal of a parent has no code. No verdict of this file records a closure.

fields.limits: A limit has kind, resource, unit and amount; its key is the first three. No vector holds a period.
fields.parents: parent.seal is the seal of the parent; notaries are the notaries that it pins; pools states one amount for a limit key. A row states its executor, its recipient in one mode, its limits, its certifier and its coin.
fields.fit: child.ordinal selects the row. A recipient by key has request_public_key alone; a recipient by name has name and owner_public_key.
fields.coins: row_coin is the coin as the row states it. node.coin_transaction is what the verifier's node gives for the transaction of that outpoint: null where it knows none; block_height null where it is pending; outputs lists the scripts of its outputs by index. child.seal is the seal outpoint that the child names, and child.anchor_inputs lists the outpoints that the inputs of its anchor spend. Two outcomes are codes of LIP-0023 for an anchor that it refuses before this profile is asked: W_ISSUANCE_SPENDS_SEAL for an input that spends the seal (C2.4), and W_LINKAGE_REQUIRED for inputs from the seal transaction that are not exactly one input on the output after the seal (C2.3). The group holds no other check of LIP-0023.
fields.ledgers: grants lists the facts of each grant: a child states its parent and its ordinal, and a parent the executor and the limits of each row. Each step is one request at one executor, with its identity, what it consumes and the expected outcome: reserved, held for an identity that already holds a reservation, or a code. end lists, for each executor that reserved something, its accounts with their amounts, in the order of the canonical form of their keys.

parents.claim: A pool of 100 and two rows of 60 and 40 at two executors. The first names its recipient by key, the second by name.
Rows of 60 and 30 under a pool of 100: the rows may leave a part of the pool unused.
Rows of 60 and 41 under a pool of 100: one atom above the pool.
A row limits a key for which the parent states no pool.
A second kind of limit in one row, with a pool of its own: each key is summed apart.
A row states two limits with the same key.
Two rows state the same coin.
The coin of a row is the seal of the parent.
Two rows name the same executor and the same recipient. Each has its own ordinal, limit and coin.
The script that a row states for its coin is a key hash and no witness key hash.
A row names a certifier that the parent does not pin.
A row states a recipient in both modes at once.
Two rows of the largest amount that the number form allows, under a pool of that amount: the sum is exact and above the pool.

fit.claim: A child of row 1 with the executor, the recipient and the limit of its row.
A child of row 1 with a smaller limit than its row.
A child of row 2, whose recipient is named by name.
A child without a limit: it can consume nothing that is counted.
The ordinal 3 under a parent with two rows.
The child names another service than its row.
The child names the service of its row with another pinned public key.
A child of row 1 that names the executor of row 2.
The child names another request key than its row.
The row names its recipient by key, and the child names a recipient by name.
A child of row 2 names the name of its row with another owner key.
The limit of the child is one atom above the limit of its row.
The child has a limit whose key its row does not have: another kind.
The child states its limit in another unit than its row, so the key is another one.
Two defects: the ordinal 3, and another executor. The ordinal is checked before any row is read.
Two defects: another executor, and a limit above the row.
Two defects: another recipient, and a limit above the row.

coins.claim: The coin is confirmed at height 650, the parent commits a recent block at height 700, and the anchor of the child spends the coin beside its linkage input and a funding input. The coin and the seal of the child are in two transactions.
The coin is confirmed in the parent's recent block itself.
The coin is confirmed one block above the parent's recent block.
The transaction of the coin is pending.
The node does not know the transaction of the coin.
The output at the stated index has another script than the row states.
The transaction of the coin has no output at the stated index.
The block that holds the coin is not on the active chain of the observation.
The anchor of the child does not spend the coin: it is funded by another confirmed output.
The anchor spends the coin of another row of the same parent.
The anchor spends another output of the transaction that holds the coin.
A second child of the row, after the issuance of the first spent the coin: its confirmed anchor cannot have that input and spends other outputs.
The accepted boundary: a reorganisation removed the first issuance, and the anchor of another child spends the coin on the chain that the verifier now validates. The facts are those of coin-01.

Two findings. The coin is output 0 of the child's seal transaction, whose output 1 is the seal and whose output 2 the linkage output, and the anchor spends the coin beside the linkage output. LIP-0023 C2.3 refuses the anchor for its two inputs from the seal transaction, before this profile is asked, and its code keeps its meaning.
Two defects: the coin is confirmed above the parent's recent block, and the anchor does not spend it. The coin is checked as the row states it before the anchor is read for it.

One input with two roles. Output 0 of a transaction is the seal of the child and output 1 a witness key hash, confirmed at height 650. The parent names output 1 as the coin of the row. The anchor of the child spends output 1 once, beside a funding input. LIP-0023 finds its one linkage input, the coin is on the chain as stated, and the anchor spends it; the coin is an output of the child's seal transaction.

Two findings: the coin is the third output of the child's seal transaction, and the anchor spends the linkage output alone and not the coin. The comparison of the two transaction ids stands before the other checks of the coin.

The control of coin-16: the same seal transaction and the same anchor, with the coin in another transaction that is confirmed at the same height. The linkage input and the input of the coin are two inputs.
Two findings: the one input with two roles of coin-16, and a seal transaction that is confirmed above the parent's recent block. The comparison of the two transaction ids is reported.

Two findings: the row names the seal of the child itself as its coin, and the anchor spends it beside the linkage output. LIP-0023 C2.4 refuses an anchor that spends the seal, before this profile is asked.

ledgers.claim: One parent with an own limit of 50 and rows of 60 and 40, over three executors. Each child spends its row in full at its executor, and the parent spends its own limit at a third. 150 are reserved, which is the own limit plus the rows, and no account of one executor is charged for a request at another.

The parent and two siblings name one service, so one ledger holds the own account of the parent and both row accounts. Direct requests of the parent and requests of the two children come in turn, each up to its ceiling. A request of a child moves no own account of the parent, and a direct request moves no row.

Two documents of row 1, each with an own limit of 60 under a row of 60. 30 under the first and 30 under the second fill the row. One atom more under either refuses for the row, and both own accounts stay as they were.
No borrowing. Row 1 has 50 of its 60 left, and row 2 is full. A request of 10 under a second document of row 2 refuses, although the rows together have 50 left under the pool.
The own account of the parent is full, and a child of the same service still spends under its row. A checker that charges the parent's own limit for a child's request refuses the second request.
A request is presented again with the same identity: it holds its reservation and is not charged a second time.
A request that holds a reservation under the first document of a row is presented again under the second document. It is not charged again, and the own account of the second document stays empty.
Two requests of 10 compete for the last 15 of a row, the first document before the second.
The same two requests in the other order: the other one is reserved. In either order one of the two is refused, and the row ends at 55.
A request consumes two limit keys, coins and model requests. The third request fits the coins and exceeds the requests: nothing of it is reserved, and the coin accounts stay as they were.
A request consumes a limit key for which its grant states no limit: the ceiling is 0, and nothing is reserved.
A child with an own limit of 0 under a row of 60: an allowance of zero authorizes nothing.
A grant that is no child and has no rows: its requests move its own account alone.
